analysis.title: "Sprinting To Stand Still": Goldman's Molavi Spots Two Of Three CapEx-Peak Signals Already Flashing
key_insights: Bobby Molavi (GS macro trader) says the last 2-3 months felt like 'sprinting to stand still': PnL volatility is high, net output is flat or negative, and moves have shifted from week-to-week to intra-week, with violent risk-on/risk-off swings at stock, sector, factor and theme level.

The S&P is at all-time highs while US fundamental L/S net exposure has fallen to about 46%, near the lowest since the April 2025 'Liberation Day' selloff. Professionals are not making money owning the index.

The gap between average single-stock realized vol and index realized vol is about 26-28 points on a 3-month basis, above the 2009 peak of about 20. Single stocks swing widely while index moves cancel out, which makes stock picking hard.

Concentration: the top 5 S&P companies have a combined market cap near $22T, about 30% of the index, equal to the weight of 434 constituents. The 2013-14 average was about 200 stocks and the 2000 dot-com peak about 350.
Performance split: AI winners +58%, S&P +13%, Nasdaq +22%, median S&P stock -15%. The 'AI 10' are roughly 40% of S&P market cap.

Liquidity is thinning while volume rises. Average daily top-of-book liquidity is down 21% since 2023 ($14M to about $11M). Top-of-book depth per $1B traded is $11K, down 93% from $162K in 2017. Daily volume has tripled since 2017 (6.5B to nearly 19B shares). In June, when volume hit a 2026 high of 22.8B shares, depth fell 33%.

Forward P/E understates valuation at tops: March 2000 forward P/E was 25.2x vs 39.3x on earned EPS and about 60x GAAP. In 2007 it was 15.1x forward vs 31.6x earned and over 100x GAAP. Molavi cites peak margins being extrapolated, over-optimistic growth, late analyst cuts and decaying earnings quality (he says he is not claiming we are at the top).

Twin-peaks framework: historically capex peaked after the equity peak by 2 years (UK railways), 1 year (US utilities), 18 months (Japan), 7 months (dotcom) and 5 months (US shale), each time signalled by a central bank policy shift and rate rises. Molavi marks equity stalling and a central bank shift/hikes as 'check', with capex still to watch. The article's author reads this as two of three signals flashing.
Goldman's chart shows hyperscaler capex growth peaking at 116% y/y in Q3 2026, then decelerating each quarter in consensus to the low 20s by end-2027.
The AI 'orbit' (megacaps, hyperscalers, neoclouds, labs, chips, compute) is sized at roughly $25-30T across public and private markets. Over $500B of debt has been issued this year to fund AI capex.

Credit is repricing AI borrowers: Oracle 5-year CDS is near a record 261bps (implying about a 20% default rate), SpaceX CDS implies 16% and Nvidia 7%. Single-name default risk was 1.3% at the start of the year vs 10.3% in 2007. Yields on some AI capex financings are rising and IG and HY are starting to move.

CDS market notional has shrunk from about $61T in 2007 to about $11T, while central bank balance sheets grew from $9T to $33.9T, which Molavi describes as the hedge shifting from private markets to public balance sheets.

Equity issuance is fatiguing: monthly US equity offerings fell from 65 in May to 24 in September, and quarterly issuance fell from a record $252B in Q2 to $93B in Q3 (still +20% y/y). Firmus, Bamboo and Oura deals were cut or pulled. Broadcom and SpaceX are signalling raises for AI capex.

AI capex financing has shifted from cash to primary equity and IPOs, with a more discerning buyer than in H1. Buybacks remain a prop: S&P 500 gross buybacks grew 20% y/y in Q2 2026 and authorizations are on track for a record year.
Rates/Europe: France is the 'epicentre' with the OAT-Bund spread at 140bps, a level not seen since 1990, with contagion fears ahead of the UK budget and Spain's snap election.

Oil: Molavi says re-routing, reserve releases and stockpile selling are running dry. Oil can go lower only if many things go right, while upside reasons grow: reserve refilling on dips, elevated shipping and insurance costs, and structurally impaired refining capacity. Jet fuel is about $1,100-1,400 by tenor vs a $700 long-term average.

Odds and ends: cyber names have outperformed YTD (Okta +155% vs S&P, Fortinet +138%, CrowdStrike +124%, Palo Alto +116%, HACK ETF +56%). GPU rental prices are up 17-21% across H100/H200/B200/B300. Retail searches for 'stocks to buy' and options are at their lowest weekly rate since August 2025 while Robinhood margin use rises. Ramp token usage hit a new high above 700 in September (100 in January) but token spend fell 5% last month. EM beat MSCI World in 6 of the last 9 market 'crashes'.

Goldman anchors on three themes (AI, oil, yields) and relies on the strength of megacaps, narrowness, earnings and belief in the future. The ZeroHedge author concludes that history usually puts the stock peak before the capex peak, and plans to revisit after hyperscaler Q3 capex reports later in October.

market_movers.rationale: Oracle 5-year CDS is near a record 261bps, up 24bps from the 237bps record set after the force majeure headline, implying about a 20% default rate.
Nvidia CDS implies a 7% default probability. Micron and Nvidia are expected to deliver a third of Q3 EPS growth.
Micron and Nvidia together are expected to deliver a third of S&P Q3 EPS growth, per the article's reference to its Oct 6 piece.
Broadcom is signalling a capital raise for AI capex as issuance windows narrow.
Outperformed the S&P by 155% YTD as cyber names lead.

sector_views.rationale: Hyperscaler capex growth is seen peaking at 116% y/y in Q3 2026. Credit spreads on AI borrowers are widening and issuance is slowing, while token volume growth supports infra demand.
The group has crushed the index YTD, with Okta, Fortinet, CrowdStrike and Palo Alto up 116-155% vs the S&P and the HACK ETF up 56%.
Jet fuel at $1,100-1,400 vs a $700 long-term average, and a squeezed consumer, make passing on costs without hurting demand doubtful.
EM beat MSCI World in 6 of the last 9 market crashes, and Molavi argues the EM trade has much further to run.

earnings_insights: Micron and Nvidia alone are expected to deliver about a third of S&P Q3 EPS growth (consensus expectation, per the article's earlier Oct 6 piece).

Forward P/E (consensus-based) is viewed as flattering: Molavi says peak margins are extrapolated and operating EPS flatters at tops, so these slip-ups will be more painful in a market of fast valuation and revenue run-rate growth.
Hyperscaler Q3 capex numbers are due later in October and are the next check on the capex-peak thesis.
S&P 500 gross buybacks grew 20% y/y in Q2 2026 (reported), with US buyback authorizations on track for a record year.

Extreme index concentration: 5 stocks carry the weight of 434.
Thin top-of-book liquidity that makes large trades hard to execute.
AI capex financing strain: over $500B of debt issued this year, rising yields on AI financings, Oracle CDS at records, and issuance windows closing.
Earnings quality decay and extrapolated peak margins that make forward P/E misleading.
France-led European bond contagion with UK budget and Spain snap election risk.
Oil upside risk as stopgap supply solutions run dry.
Falling revenue per token, since token spend fell 5% while usage rose (author's view).
